text:
olivia: Heads-up — automated qa-factcheck eval spiked after we switched the default deployment profile to the awq-int8-hybrid (v2-hybrid). Accuracy went from ~96% down to ~81% on the same prompt set. Noticed the failures cluster on outputs that include fenced code blocks and inline JSON.

kevin: can you paste the eval diff + the serving config you used?

olivia: here's the minimal config we used on the dedicated pool:
```json
{
  \"model\": \"open-llm-2-13b\",
  \"profile\": \"awq-int8-hybrid\",
  \"batch_size\": 8,
  \"kv_cache\": true,
  \"max_seq\": 4096,
  \"tokenizer\": \"hf-fast\"
}
```
and a failing example from the eval harness (expected vs actual):
```
EXPECTED:
```json
{
  \"source\": \"wikipedia:AtomicNumber\",
  \"answer\": \"The atomic number of helium is 2.\"
}
```
ACTUAL:
```json
{
  \"source\": \"wikipedia:AtomicNumber\",
  \"answer\": \"The atomic number of helium is 2.\\n\\\`\\\`\\\`\nSome extra citation text.\"
}
```
```
The unexpected trailing escaped backticks and an extra newline show up only when the output contains fenced code.

tara: interesting. did we also change any runtime/compile kernels recently? batching or streaming logic?

olivia: not on the model-serving side that I know of — the runtime change that went out last week was a small batching optimization for continuous batching. I can repro locally if I force the harness to use the dedicated pool.

ben: my hunch — something in the AWQ dequant + batching hot path is touching the detokenization boundary incorrectly. Might be a buffer overlap when multiple requests are batched and the decoder writes escape sequences into a shared output buffer. Try batch=1 and kv_cache=false to see if it disappears.

maria: also check tokenizer variant. hf-fast (tokenizers in Rust) sometimes behaves slightly differently on decode than HF python. For structured outputs we usually use the slow python tokenizer to match eval tooling.

kevin: i reran the harness with batch_size=1 and kv_cache=false on the same model/profile — spike disappears, accuracy back to ~95.7%. So it's definitely a batching/kv interaction.

olivia: logging snippet from a failing run (trimmed):
```
DECODE TOKENS: [313, 92, 440, 198, 220]
DECODED STR: "2.\\n\\\`\\\`\\\`\nSome extra citation text"
EXPECT NO ESCAPED BACKTICKS
```
Token id 92 is showing up where we didn't expect a backslash.

tara: that token id (92) is backslash in the vocab? if a chunk boundary is inserted, the decoder may add an escape. We should compare raw logits / token ids across the batch lanes before detokenization. If the tokens are correct but detokenizer mixes buffers, that's different than a quantization error.

ben: i'll start a bisect across the runtime changes that touched batching (range: commit a1f3..b4d2). plan: reproduce minimal failing case, then step through commits. assigning to myself.

maria: i'll run the tokenizer parity checks (hf-fast vs hf-slow) on the failing sample and also run a quant-sim that uses fp32 decode with AWQ quant params to see if decode tokens differ.

ci-bot: ci:eval-harness queued (job id: 86723) — reproducer with batch=8 and batch=1 will run, notify on completion.

kevin: good call on tokenizer parity. if tokenizer differences are a contributor we should pin the tokenizer in the deployment profile. Also consider a fast-path guard: disable AWQ batching when output contains triple-backtick tokens until we have fix.

olivia: thanks — i'll collect the eval diffs + a minimal repro and open a bug with the reproducer and the failing token sequence. tagging @ben and @maria for follow-up. :eyes:
